Navigating a child's history of severe trauma alongside challenging behaviors at school can be incredibly stressful. To answer your question directly, yes, it would be highly beneficial to seek therapy for her. Even if her suicidal statements appear to be a way to avoid assignments or seek attention, they indicate that she is struggling to communicate her needs and cope with her emotions. Given her trauma history, a mental health professional can help her process those underlying experiences and teach her healthier ways to ask for support or manage stress. 

Furthermore, any mention of suicide should always be taken seriously and evaluated by a professional to ensure her safety, as it can be difficult to know exactly what she is feeling inside. A therapist can provide a safe space for her and offer you guidance on how to respond effectively. If you ever become concerned for her immediate safety, please reach out to emergency services or call or text the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988.
